sketches.title: The Wrong Button
sketches.premise: A tiny home mistake starts a chain of household trouble. Take turns pressing, touching, or choosing one thing that causes the next thing; the host explains the growing mess with a straight face and a small jab.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if one clear household action happens because of the standing problem, adds a new problem, and leaves a physical or digital thing for the other player to affect; a skipped result, a clean fix or final rescue, an undo, or a newcomer who changes the scene without being caused fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one plain next event beginning with “Then,” naming the action and its result; example: “Then the remote slips under the sofa, so the TV jumps to the loudest channel.”
sketches.first_card: Then a thumb hits the wrong button on the washing machine, and it starts filling with hot water.

sketches.title: The Leak Line
sketches.premise: At home, one small leak spreads through rooms, objects, and bad choices. Each player adds exactly one place or item the water reaches next, while the host gives earnest safety notes that become less useful by the turn.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if the water reaches one new connected thing because of the standing wetness and creates a fresh target, while a jump to an unconnected room, a full repair or dry ending, reversing the flow, or adding a person or event that could not be reached fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one next spread of the leak, starting with “Then,” and name the visible link; example: “Then the puddle runs under the mat, soaking the keys hidden beneath it.”
sketches.first_card: Then a bead of water slips from the loose pipe beneath the kitchen sink.

sketches.title: The Stain Chain
sketches.premise: A tiny mark at home travels through clothes, furniture, cleaning tools, and desperate cover-ups. Players take turns making one honest change to the stain; the host offers gentle explanations and judges the stain, not your tragic laundry skills.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if one new stain or cleaning effect results directly from the standing mark and gives the next player something visible to worsen, while a missing transfer, a spotless ending, a reversal that removes the mark, or an unrelated person or place fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one next stain event beginning with “Then,” naming what transfers and where; example: “Then the wet sleeve brushes the sofa, leaving a dark hand-shaped patch.”
sketches.first_card: Then a spoonful of red sauce lands on the clean shirt hanging over the chair.

sketches.title: The Assembly Error
sketches.premise: A harmless home project is built one wrong step at a time. Players add exactly one new mistake to the object or the room, and the host reads the instructions with earnest confidence while quietly roasting the inventor.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if one physical change is caused by the current build mistake, makes the object less usable or the room more unsafe, and leaves a new part to mishandle; skipping a needed build change, finishing safely, undoing a part, or bringing in a specialist who solves it fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one next construction mistake beginning with “Then,” showing the part and its result; example: “Then the shelf is tightened backward, so its top leans toward the open paint tin.”
sketches.first_card: Then the first screw goes into the flat-pack shelf, but the board is facing the wrong way.

sketches.title: The Sound Next Door
sketches.premise: One small home noise turns into a louder, stranger household event. Each move adds one sound caused by the last sound or by what it shakes, and the host gives calm commentary as the house loses its dignity.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if one new audible event is caused by the standing sound through vibration, reaction, or a nearby object, and creates a clear sound for the next player; silence, a concert-like jump, a total quiet ending, an undo, or an unrelated newcomer fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one next sound event beginning with “Then,” naming what makes it and what the sound changes; example: “Then the rattling vent shakes a spoon from the counter, and it clatters into the dog bowl.”
sketches.first_card: Then a dropped coin rolls beneath the radiator, making a thin metal rattle.

sketches.title: The Fridge Fiasco
sketches.premise: A small fridge mishap turns dinner into a home-grown disaster. Players take turns changing one food, shelf, container, or kitchen surface because of what stands; the host stays earnest, explains each cause, and treats your cooking plan like evidence.
sketches.criterion: A move follows if one new kitchen mess is directly caused by the standing food or spill, makes another food or surface vulnerable, and keeps the same kitchen scene; a skipped spill or transfer, a finished meal or complete cleanup, undoing the mess, or an impossible new visitor fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write one next kitchen event beginning with “Then,” naming the food and its plain effect; example: “Then the tipped yogurt runs across the shelf and under the open jar of mustard.”
sketches.first_card: Then the fridge door swings open, and a cup of yogurt wobbles on the top shelf.
